title: Mentored On-call Bootcamp and Runbook Autogen Playbook
author: Anika Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook describes a two-track operational program: (1) a mentored on-call bootcamp designed to accelerate new responders from shadow to solo-ready; and (2) a lightweight runbook autogeneration workflow that produces focused incident runbooks from signal templates and service metadata. The combined program reduces time-to-competence for new responders while ensuring runbooks remain current and concise.

Who should use this page

- New SREs and backend engineers joining on-call rotations.
- Team leads running game days or mentorship cohorts.
- Runbook owners responsible for operational runbook upkeep.

Scope and goals

- Scope: Redwood Inference hosted services (inference-gateway, batch-router, kv-cache, model-fallback), and the public status page flow. Private/Dedicated customer on-call processes are out of scope for this document; see eng-private-deployments for customer-specific runbooks.
- Goals: reduce first-solo mean-time-to-stabilize (MTTS) from 21 days to <=10 days; ensure every production runbook is < 2 pages and can be autogenerated from templates in <=15 minutes; create a repeatable gameday syllabus with measurable scoring.

Core components summary

1) Mentored Bootcamp — 2-week curriculum combining shadow shifts, progressive responsibility, and coach-led reviews.
2) Runbook Autogen — CLI + templating pipeline that pulls service metadata (owner, SLOs, primary signals) and emits a runnable incident playbook file.
3) Gameday Syllabus — four reproducible scenarios (throttle, KV-coldstart, model-degradation, multi-region failover) with pass/fail scoring.

Roles & responsibilities

- Primary Responder (Responder): accepts pager, performs triage, executes runbook checklist.
- Mentor (Coach): senior responder assigned to a mentee cohort; joins critical incidents and signs off on first 3 solo incidents.
- Bridge Lead: coordinates stakeholders during medium+ incidents (severity >= SEV2).
- Runbook Owner: maintains runbook content and reviews autogenerated drafts monthly.
- Incident Recorder: records timeline, SLO evidence, and customer messages during the incident.

Mentored Bootcamp: structure and schedule

Week 0 (Pre-boarding)
- Read: operator quick-start, service SLOs, privilege/access checklist.
- Setup: ensure MFA, VPN, pager, slack, and status-page write access are working.

Week 1 (Shadow + Guided Triage)
- Day 1–3: Shadow primary responder during two low-severity incidents. Mentor demonstrates triage; mentee performs evidence collection.
- Day 4: Micro-gameday 1 — simulated KV-cache coldstart (see scenario A). Mentor scores.
- Day 5: Review session: checklist audit and runbook familiarity test.

Week 2 (Progressive Autonomy)
- Days 6–9: Mentee accepts low-severity pages with Mentor on standby (not on bridge).
- Day 10: Mentee leads a medium-severity simulated incident with a cross-functional bridge.
- Graduation: Mentor signs off if MTTS on supervised incidents < baseline threshold and checklist pass rate >= 90%.

Mentorship signals and escalation thresholds

- Mentor must be paged automatically when:
  - Error rate for inference-gateway > 0.5% for 5m (production),
  - Latency p95 over 500ms for 10m,
  - Any SEV1 or suspected data corruption.
- If mentee initiates escalation, the Mentor must respond within 10 minutes during bootcamp.

Runbook Autogen workflow (high level)

1) Metadata sources: service manifest (service-name, owners, pager-team), SLO document, alert rules (Prometheus), and recent RCA notes.
2) Template engine: runbook-template.yaml uses placeholders: {{service}}, {{primary_signals}}, {{first_steps}}, {{rollback}}.
3) CLI command (example):
   ./ops-tool runbook generate --service inference-gateway --output /tmp/inference-gateway-runbook.md
4) Post-process: Runbook Owner reviews autogenerated draft within 3 business days and marks as canonical or iterates.

Autogen example template (snippet)

---
title: "{{service}} - Incident Runbook (autogen)"
owners: "{{owners}}"
primary_signals:
  - "p95_latency"
  - "5m_error_rate"
first_steps:
  - "Identify impacted routes: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings"
  - "Check KV cache health: kubectl get sts kv-cache -n prod"
  - "If model-fallback engaged: confirm fallback model is healthy"
rollback:
  - "Revert latest config deploy if correlated within 30m"
---

Operational runbooks — minimal required sections

Every production runbook (autogen or manual) must include the following sections and content:

1) Title, service tag, owners (pager/team), runbook owner, last_review_date.
2) SLO summary: availability % and latency p95 target. Example: "Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly; Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for hosted-api routes."
3) Primary signals and dashboards to inspect (direct URLs).
4) Rapid triage checklist (Top 10 actions in order).
5) Containment actions and temporary mitigations (toggle flags, traffic shaping).
6) Escalation matrix with contacts and time-to-respond thresholds.
7) Post-incident owner and RCA link placeholder.

Example Rapid triage checklist (short-form)

1. Acknowledge the page and set status: "Investigating" on status.redwood.com.
2. Identify impacted tenant scope using the request-id header pattern.
3. Check downstream dependencies: kv-cache, batch-router queues, model-fallback.
4. If p95 latency > 500ms: enable short-term traffic shed on batch-router.
5. If errors increasing > 1% and persisting 5m: trigger bridge and page Mentor.

Escalation matrix (table)

| Role | When to page | Channel | Response SLA |
| Bridge Lead | SEV2+ or multi-team | Pager + Slack #ops-bridge | 5 min |
| Mentor | Bootcamp mentee escalations or SEV1 | Pager | 10 min |
| Runbook Owner | Runbook integrity concerns | Email + Slack | 1 business day |
| Oncall Manager | > 2h unresolved SEV2 | Phone call | 15 min |

Game day syllabus and scoring

Four standard scenarios (each 60–90 minutes):

A) KV coldstart under load
- Objective: validate cache warmup procedures and autoscaler behavior.
- Success criteria: MTTS < 30 min; p95 returns < 350ms within autoscale window.

B) Token-throttle spike (noisy tenant)
- Objective: test tenant-aware rate-limiting and quick-blacklist workflow.
- Success criteria: noisy tenant isolated within 10 minutes; no >5% collateral latency increase for others.

C) Model-quality regression (score drift)
- Objective: exercise model-fallback, rollback, and canary rollback process.
- Success criteria: fallback enabled and user-visible quality restored in < 20 minutes.

D) Multi-region failover
- Objective: validate routing, capacity ramp, and customer notices across regions.
- Success criteria: automated failover triggers and customer status posted in <15 minutes; no data loss.

Scoring rubric (per scenario): pass if >= 80 points of 100. Points assigned across: triage speed (30), containment (30), communications (20), post-incident artifacts (20).

Customer status and comms templates

Guidelines
- Use brand-safe language (non-technical first paragraph).
- Declare impact, affected areas, mitigation steps, ETA, and next update cadence.
- Avoid speculative root causes; be transparent on what is known and what is being investigated.

Initial acknowledgement template (status page / email)

Subject: Investigation: Degraded inference performance for some requests\nMessage:
We are investigating an issue affecting inference response times for a subset of requests. Engineering is actively investigating. Impact: intermittent elevated latency for hosted API routes in us-west-2. Mitigation: routing changes and cache warmup are in progress. Next update: in 15 minutes.

Escalation update template (when containment in progress)

Subject: Update: Progress on containment for inference latency issue

Message:
We have isolated the cause to increased KV cache misses from a backend deploy. We have rolled forward a temporary routing rule to divert traffic away from the affected nodes; this is reducing latency for most customers. We are continuing to validate and expect a more complete mitigation within 60 minutes.

Resolution & RCA placeholder template

Subject: Resolved: Inference latency issue — summary and next steps

Message:
The incident is resolved. Root cause: configuration change that increased cache eviction frequency during a specific traffic pattern. Impact: 0.3% of requests experienced elevated latency; no data loss. Actions taken: reverted the change, increased cache headroom config, and scheduled a follow-up rollout with a canary window. RCA link: [RCA document URL]

Post-incident debriefs and artifacts

Required artifacts for closure (must exist before incident is considered closed):
- Timeline with timestamps and evidence links.
- SLO impact report (error budget consumed).
- Postmortem (RCA) with owner and remediation actions; remediation must have an owner and ETA.
- Runbook updates or autogen iteration to prevent recurrence.

Post-incident review cadence

- For SEV1/SEV2 incidents: schedule a 60min postmortem review within 7 days; reviewers: service owner, SRE mentor, product manager.
- For bootcamp mentees: the Mentor performs a focused coaching session within 3 days covering decisions made and gap areas.

Runbook review policy

- Autogenerated drafts: reviewed within 3 business days.
- Canonical runbooks: reviewed quarterly and after any SEV2+ incident affecting the service.

Appendix: example status page PATCH payload (curl)

curl -X PATCH https://status.redwood.com/api/v1/incidents/INC-12345 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status":"investigating","body":"Investigating elevated inference latency for some requests. Next update in 15 minutes."}'

Appendix: bootcamp scoring checklist (quick)

- [ ] Completed 3 shadow shifts
- [ ] Led 2 low-severity pages with Mentor on standby
- [ ] Passed micro-gameday scenario A or B
- [ ] Demonstrated runbook edit and status-posting capability
